rows.note: This is the all-purpose Cantonese noun for a mathematical mean or average.

example.english: The mean score for this class is eighty.
example.traditional: 呢班同學嘅平均數係八十分。
example.jyutping: ni1 baan1 tung4 hok6 ge3 ping4 gwan1 sou3 hai6 baat3 sap6 fan1

rows.note: For an unkind person or action, this is the all-purpose spoken choice; it can also describe something shabby, inferior, or malicious.

example.english: The way they treat people is really mean.
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam3 joeng6 deoi3 jan4 zan1 hai6 hou2 seoi1

rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose choice when “mean” identifies what something signifies or indicates, including an inferred meaning.

example.english: I take this symbol to mean “Caution: slippery floor,” telling people to walk slowly.
example.traditional: 我將呢個符號理解為小心地滑，即係叫人行慢啲。
example.jyutping: ngo5 zoeng1 ni1 go3 fu4 hou6 lei5 gaai2 wai4 siu2 sam1 dei6 waat6 zik1 hai6 giu3 jan4 haang4 maan6 di1

rows.note: Use this for intending or planning to do something, including a benevolent intention such as meaning well.

example.english: I mean to take my mum for dim sum on Sunday.
example.traditional: 我諗住星期日帶阿媽去飲茶。
example.jyutping: ngo5 nam2 zyu6 sing1 kei4 jat6 daai3 aa3 maa1 heoi3 jam2 caa4

rows.note: Use this specifically for someone who is ungenerous with money or gifts.

example.english: They always count every penny when shopping; they’re really mean.
example.traditional: 佢買嘢成日計到足，真係孤寒。
example.jyutping: keoi5 maai5 je5 sing4 jat6 gai3 dou3 zuk1 zan1 hai6 gu1 hon4

rows.note: Use this when a speaker is referring to the comment or idea they intend to express.

example.english: What I mean is, this method is really quite convenient.
example.traditional: 我想講，呢個方法真係幾方便。
example.jyutping: ngo5 soeng2 gong2 ni1 go3 fong1 faat3 zan1 hai6 gei2 fong1 bin6

rows.note: Use this when “mean” means average or typical, as in an average family or ordinary result.

example.english: The mean score for this class is average, not high.
example.traditional: 呢班平均分一般，唔算高。
example.jyutping: ni1 baan1 ping4 gwan1 fan1 jat1 bun1 m4 syun3 gou1

rows.note: Use this when asking or stating whether someone sincerely holds the view they expressed.

example.jyutping: nei5 zan1 hai6 gam3 nam2 gaa3

rows.note: Use this when “mean” describes a problem or task as difficult or tricky.

example.english: This is a mean maths problem.
example.jyutping: ni1 tiu4 sou3 hok6 tai4 gei2 naan4 gaa3
